options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
4.sol: Protostele is the simplest and considered to be the most primitive type of stele. It consists of a solid core of xylem surrounded by the cylinder of phloem, enclosing no pith. 32408.sol: Ferric chloride is a hemostatic agent, which means that it can be used to stop bleeding by promoting the coagulation of blood. 44763.subject: Botany
44763.text: Consider following statements and Choose correct ones from given options. I. Shark do not have any bone in its body. II. Water snake and salamander belongs to same class and have largest RBC. III. Silver fish is a true fish while cuttle and star fishes are molluscs and echinoderms respectively. IV. Ornithorhynchus is a connecting link between reptiles and mammals.
44763.sol: - Shark is a member of Chondrichthyes class, which is a cartilaginous fish. - Water snake is a reptile and salamander is an amphibian having largest RBC in animal kingdom. - Silver fish (Lepisma) is an arthropod, cuttle fish (Sepia) is a mollusc and star fish (Asterias) is an echinodermate. So none of them is a true fish (Pisces). - Ornithorhychus is a mammal which is also known as duck-billed playtypus. It is a member of Monotremata order which is a connecting link between reptiles and mammals.

55755.subject: Chemistry
55755.text: Identify correct order for repulsion between electron pair present in valence shell of central atom of molecule?
55755.sol: According to VSEPR theory, the electron pairs in the valence shell of the central atom repel each other to minimize electron-electron repulsion. Lone pairs (Lp) are localized on the central atom and are attracted by only one nucleus, so they occupy more space and exert greater repulsion. Bond pairs (Bp) are shared between two atoms and are attracted by two nuclei, so they occupy less space and exert lesser repulsion. Thus, the correct order of repulsion between electron pairs is Lp-Lp > Lp-Bp > Bp-Bp . Answer: Lp-L

For a general reaction aA + bB cC + dD , the rate is defined as Rate = - 1 a d[A] dt = - 1 b d[B] dt = + 1 c d[C] dt = + 1 d d[D] dt . Given the rate expression - 1 2 d[x] dt = - d[y] dt = 1 2 d[z] dt , the stoichiometric coefficients are determined by the denominators. The negative terms indicate reactants, while the positive term indicates a product. The balanced reaction must be 2x + y 2z , which corresponds to option B .

The effect of genetic drift is more significant in large populations.
Sometimes a few individuals become isolated from large populations and produce a small new population in a new
71102.sol: Genetic drift refers to the random fluctuations in allele frequencies from one generation to the next. It is a directionless process. It is also known as the Sewall Wright effect. The effect of genetic drift is highly significant in small populations, not large populations, because random changes have a much larger proportional impact when the number of individuals is small. 72549.sol: The error lies in part (3) of the given sentence. The past perfect tense 'had taken' is incorrectly used with the definite past time adverb 'yesterday'. 79349.sol: In old trees, the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown due to deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils in the central or innermost layers of the stem. 84852.sol: In prokaryotes, such as, E. coli , DNA being negatively charged is held with some proteins that have positive charges in a region termed as ‘nucleoid’. 121903.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Isogamy has gametes that are non-flagellated but similar in size. Reason: Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in some species termed as anisogamous.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
121903.sol: Isogamous is non-flagellated but similar in size. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in some species of Chlamydomonas is termed as anisogamous.

121915.subject: Botany
121915.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown. Reason: The shades of phaeophyceae depends upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
121915.sol: Phaeophyceae vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them.

122068.subject: Botany
122068.text: Haploids are more suitable for mutation studies than the diploids. This is because
options: All mutations, whether dominant or recessive are expressed in haploids
Haploids are reproductively more stable than diploids
Mutagens penetrate in haploids more effectively than diploids
Haploids are more abundant in nature than diploids
122068.sol: Haploids have only one set of chromosome hence alleles.

123044.subject: Botany
123044.text: In a certain plant, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the base of the stem. Which type of leaf venation is typically observed in plants possessing this type of root system?
123044.sol: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system (e.g., wheat). Monocots typically exhibit parallel venation in their leaves. In contrast, dicots generally have a tap root system and exhibit reticulate venation. Therefore, a plant with a fibrous root system will typically show parallel venation. Answer: Parallel venation

123113.subject: Botany
123113.text: Which of the following is a correct pair?
123113.sol: Cuscuta commonly known as dodder is a parasitic plant. It belongs to order Solanales and family -Convolvulaceae. Dischidia is an epiphytic plant that grow on supports such as tree trunks or branches. Opuntia commonly called prickly pear is xerophytic plants, consisting thorns. Capsella also called as Shepherd's purse is a genus of herbaceous plant and biennial plants in the family Brassicaceae.

123502.subject: Botany
123502.sol: Secondary meristem are the meristem that are formed secondarly from the permanent tissue. Healing of wound in plant take place by the activity of secondary meristem.

123643.subject: Botany
123643.text: In which organism does mitosis lead to the formation of syncytium?
123643.sol: Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get d

123803.subject: Botany
123803.text: It is observed that heart cells do not exhibit cell division. Such cells do not divide further and exit phase to enter an inactive stage called the cell cycle. Name the cycle.
123803.sol: These cells that do not divide further exit the G0 phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage (G0) of the cell cycle. The G0 stage of a cell denotes the exit of a cell from the cell cycle.

123993.subject: Botany
123993.text: What is the function of ribosomes in prokaryotic cells?
123993.sol: In prokaryotes, ribosomes are associated with the plasma membrane of the cell. They are about 15 nm by 20 nm in size and are made of two subunits - 50S and 30S units which when present together form 70S prokaryotic ribosomes . Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain calledpolyribosomes or polysome . The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.

124575.subject: Botany
124575.text: What process do gibberellins promote in plants with a rosette habit?
124575.sol: Gibberellins also promotes bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit .Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production.

124584.subject: Botany
124584.text: What is one of the effects of ethylene on seedlings?
124584.sol: Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR. It is synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits. Influences of ethylene on plants include horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings

125130.subject: Botany
125130.text: Fermentation Processes Characteristics A. Alcohol Fermentation 1. Produces lactic acid and occurs in animal cells during exercise. B. Lactic Acid Fermentation 2. Produces ethanol and CO2, catalyzed by pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase. C. Pyruvic Acid Decarboxylase 3. Enzyme involved in converting pyruvic acid to ethanol and CO2. D. Lactate Dehydrogenase 4. Enzyme involved in converting pyruvic aci
125130.sol: A - 2: Alcohol fermentation produces ethanol and CO2, catalyzed by pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase. B - 1: Lactic acid fermentation produces lactic acid and occurs in animal cells during exercise. C - 3: Pyruvic acid decarboxylase is an enzyme that converts pyruvic acid to ethanol and CO2. D - 4: Lactate dehydrogenase is the enzyme that converts pyruvic acid to lactic acid.

125205.subject: Botany
125205.text: The enzyme decarboxylase catalyses the following step
options: conversion of citric acid to cis aconitic acid
125205.sol: Oxalosuccinate is decarboxylated to form -ketoglutarate through the enzyme decarboxylase. It is one of the step involved in Krebs' cycle. It releases one molecule of CO ₂ . aligned & Oxalosuccinate Decarboxylase Mg ²⁺ & -ketoglutarate + CO ₂ & aligned

125650.subject: Botany
125650.text: A specific plant pigment shows a broad absorption peak in the blue region of the visible spectrum but shows absolutely no absorption in the red region. What would be the colour of this pigment when separated on a paper chromatogram?
125650.sol: According to the absorption spectrum of photosynthetic pigments, chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b show absorption peaks in both the blue and red regions of the visible spectrum. Carotenoids, however, show absorption only in the blue region and do not absorb in the red region. Therefore, the pigment described is a carotenoid. When separated by paper chromatography, carotenoids appear yellow to yellow-orange. Chlorophyll a appears bright or blue-green, and chlorophyll b appears yellow-green. Answer: Yellow to yellow-o

126081.subject: Botany
126081.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar Reason: Insects are attracted to flowers by colour and fragrance
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126081.sol: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar . Animals are attracted to flowers by colour and fragrance

126275.subject: Botany
126275.text: In some cereals such as wheat, the pollen grains lose viability within approximately what duration after their release?
126275.sol: According to NCERT, in some cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release. In contrast, members of families like Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae maintain pollen viability for months. The other options represent incorrect timeframes or confuse the viability of cereals with that of dicot families. Answer: 30 minutes

126364.subject: Botany
126364.text: Masses of pollen grains, i.e., pollinia is found in
126364.sol: Pollinia is a coherent mass of pollen grains. They are the product of only one anther lobe, but are transferred during pollination as a single unit. This is found in orchids (Orchidaceae).

126564.subject: Botany
126564.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic group as substituents on the same carbon i.e., the α-carbon. Reason: Hence, they are called α-amino acids.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
126564.sol: Amino acids are organic compounds containing an amino group and an acidic group as substituents on the same carbon i.e., the α-carbon. Hence, they are called α-amino acids.

126932.subject: Botany
126932.text: Which one of the following structural formula of two organic compounds is correctly identified along with its related function?
options: A-lecithin - a component of cell membrane
B-adenine - a nucleotide that makes up nucleic
126932.sol: 'A' is a structural formula of lecithin. It is probably the most common phospholipid. Phospholipids are major components in the lipid bilayers of cell membrane.

127224.subject: Botany
127224.text: What percentage of the earth's land area do biodiversity hotspots cover?
127224.sol: These hotspots are also regions of accelerated habitat loss. Three of these hotspots – Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Himalaya – cover our country’s exceptionally high biodiversity regions. Although all the biodiversity hotspots put together cover less than 2 per cent of the earth’s land area , the number of species they collectively harbour is extremely high and strict protection of these hotspots could reduce the ongoing mass extinctions by almost 30 per cent.

127633.subject: Botany
127633.sol: However, there are certain limitations of ecological pyramids such as it does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels. It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature; it does not accommodate a food web. Moreover , saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

127993.subject: Zoology
127993.text: What is the cloaca used for in frogs?
options: Passing faecal matter, urine, and sperms
Passing faecal matter and urine only
127993.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes , which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes. They enter the kidneys on their side and open into Bidder’s canal. Finally it communicates with the urinogenital duct that comes out of the kidneys and opens into the cloaca. The cloaca is a small, median chamber that is u

128230.subject: Zoology
128230.text: What will happen if ligaments are torn?
options: Bone less movable at joint and pain
Bone will move freely at joint and no pain
128230.sol: Ligaments join a bone with another bone in movable/synovial joints. Torn ligaments make movement at joints very painful and restricted. It heals only after prolonged movement restriction.

129351.subject: Zoology
129351.text: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is present in the subarachnoid space of the human central neural system. Based on the anatomical sequence of the cranial meninges, this space is located between which of the following two layers?
129351.sol: The cranial meninges consist of three layers: the outer dura mater, the middle arachnoid, and the inner pia mater. The term "subarachnoid" indicates a position beneath the arachnoid layer. Therefore, the subarachnoid space lies between the middle layer (arachnoid) and the innermost layer (pia mater). The space between the dura mater and arachnoid is the subdural space, while the space between the cranium (skull) and dura mater is the epidural space. Answer: Arachnoid and Pia mater

129432.subject: Zoology
129432.sol: The function of Eustachian tube is to equalise air pressure on both the sides (external and middle ear) of tympanic membrane. Thus, it connects middle ear with external ear.

129581.subject: Zoology
129581.text: What is added to the blood drained from an artery during hemodialysis?
129581.sol: Malfunctioning of kidneys can lead to accumulation of urea in blood, a condition called uremia, which is highly harmful and may lead to kidney failure. In such patients, urea can be removed by a process called hemodialysis. During the process of haemodialysis, the blood drained from a convenient artery is pumped into a dialysing unit called artificial kidney.. Blood drained from a convenient artery is pumped into a dialysing unit after adding an anticoagulant like heparin. The unit contains a coiled cellophane tube

129637.subject: Zoology
129637.text: Nephron Part Function A. Glomerulus 1. Reabsorption of water B. Proximal Convoluted Tubule 2. Filtration of blood C. Loop of Henle 3. Concentration of urine D. Collecting Duct 4. Reabsorption of ions
129637.sol: The glomerulus is involved in the filtration of blood. The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) plays a role in the reabsorption of ions. The Loop of Henle is crucial for the reabsorption of water. The collecting duct helps in the concentration of urine.

129921.subject: Zoology
129921.text: What is the role of oxygen in the respiration process?
options: To create pressure gradients between the atmosphere and the alveoli
To estimate air volume in inspiration and expiration
129921.sol: Oxygen provides energy to cells during respiration. As you have read earlier, oxygen (O2) is utilised by the organisms to indirectly break down simple molecules like glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, etc., to derive energy to perform various activities . Carbon dioxide (CO2) which is harmful is also released during the above catabolic reactions. It is, therefore, evident that O2 has to be continuously provided to the cells and CO2 produced by the cells have to be released out . This process of exchange of O2 from

130017.subject: Zoology
130017.text: Lung volume Clinical reserve A. Vital Capacity 1. Volume of air remaining after normal exhalation B. Residual Volume 2. Indicator of respiratory muscle strength C. Functional Residual Capacity 3. Maximum volume of air the lungs can hold D. Total Lung Capacity 4. Cannot be measured by spirometry
130017.sol: Vital capacity is an indicator of respiratory muscle strength. Residual volume cannot be measured by spirometry. Functional residual capacity is the volume of air remaining after normal exhalation. Total lung capacity is the maximum volume of air the lungs can hold.

130287.subject: Zoology
130287.text: What type of joint is the joint between the adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column?
130287.sol: Joints are essential for all types of movements involving the bony parts of the body. Locomotory movements are no exception to this. Force generated by the muscles is used to carry out movement through joints..The flat skull bones fuse end-to-end with the help of dense fibrous connective tissues in the form of sutures, to form the cranium, this type of joint is called fibrous joint. The joint between the adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column is of the cartilaginous type, where the bones involved are joined tog

130471.subject: Zoology
130471.text: The flat skull bones fuse end-to-end to form the cranium, creating a joint that does not allow any movement. Identify the category of this joint and the specific tissue involved in its formation.
options: Synovial joint; dense regular connective tissue
Fibrous joint; dense fibrous connective tissues
130471.sol: According to NCERT, fibrous joints do not allow any movement. This type of joint is shown by the flat skull bones which fuse end-to-end with the help of dense fibrous connective tissues in the form of sutures, to form the cranium. Cartilaginous joints involve cartilages and permit limited movement. Synovial joints are characterised by the presence of a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces of the two bones and allow considerable movement. Loose connective tissue is not the structural compon

130700.subject: Zoology
130700.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Induced abortion is also known as tubectomy 2. Vasectomy has rate of reversibility 3. Nausea is a side effect of using certain contraceptive methods 4. MTP is performed before using contraceptive measures
130700.sol: Possible ill-effects of contraceptives are nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding or even breast cancer.

131125.subject: Zoology
131125.text: Structure Function A. Epididymis 1. Storage of sperm B. Vas deferens 2. Transport of sperm C. Prostate gland 3. Secretion of fluid that nourishes sperm D. Seminal vesicles 4. Secretion of alkaline fluid
131125.sol: Epididymis: Stores sperm. Vas deferens: Transports sperm. Prostate gland: Secretes an alkaline fluid. Seminal vesicles: Secretes fluid that nourishes sperm.

131185.subject: Zoology
131185.text: The membranous cover of the ovum at ovulation is
131185.sol: The membranous cover of the ovum at ovulation is corona radiata.

131388.subject: Zoology
131388.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the i gene in the lac operon?
options: It requires the presence of lactose for its transcription.
It codes for the enzyme beta-galactosidase.
It shares a common promoter with the structural genes z, y, and a.
131388.sol: The i gene of the lac operon codes for the repressor protein and has its own promoter, separate from the structural genes (z, y, a). It is expressed constitutively , i.e. continuously and independent of lactose. It does not code for beta-galactosidase (that is the z gene). Hence the correct statement is that gene i is constitutively expressed.

131717.subject: Zoology
131717.text: Scientists Contributions A. Frederick Griffith 1. Demonstrated DNA as the genetic material using transformation B. Gregor Mendel 2. Established basic laws of inheritance through pea plant experiments C. Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty 3. Discovered the phenomenon of bacterial transformation D. Thomas Hunt Morgan 4. Demonstrated that genes are located on chromosomes
131717.sol: A - 3: Frederick Griffith discovered the phenomenon of bacterial transformation. B - 2: Gregor Mendel established the basic laws of inheritance through his experiments with pea plants. C - 1: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty demonstrated DNA as the genetic material by identifying the transforming principle. D - 4: Thomas Hunt Morgan demonstrated that genes are located on chromosomes.

131856.subject: Zoology
131856.text: Consider the following double-stranded DNA sequence of a transcription unit: Strand I: 5' - A T G C A T G - 3' Strand II: 3' - T A C G T A C - 5' If the promoter is located towards the 5' end of Strand I, what will be the sequence of the transcribed mRNA?
options: 5' - C A U G C A U - 3'
3' - U A C G U A C - 5'
5' - A T G C A T G - 3'
5' - A U G C A U G - 3'
131856.sol: According to the conventions for defining a transcription unit, the promoter is located towards the 5' end of the coding strand. Since the promoter is located at the 5' end of Strand I, Strand I is the coding strand and Strand II is the template strand. The mRNA is transcribed from the template strand (Strand II) and has a sequence complementary to it, which makes it identical to the coding strand (Strand I), except that thymine (T) is replaced by uracil (U). Coding strand (Strand I): 5' - A T G C A T G - 3' Transc

132400.subject: Zoology
132400.text: Chromosome Combination Outcome/Gender A. XY 1. Male in humans B. XX 2. Female in birds C. ZZ 3. Male in birds D. ZW 4. Female in humans
132400.sol: XY system: Males have XY chromosomes, females have XX chromosomes. ZW system: Males have ZZ chromosomes, females have ZW chromosomes. XO system: Males have one sex chromosome (XO), females have two (XX). Haplodiploidy: Males are haploid, females are diploid.

132529.subject: Zoology
132529.text: Assertion : The strength of linkage will be more when the distance between two genes is greater. Reason : Crossing over will be relatively less frequent for distantly located genes.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
132529.sol: The strength of linkage will be determined by the distance between two genes. The greater this distance, lower will be the linked strength. Crossing over will be relatively more frequent, if distance between two genes is more.

132532.subject: Zoology
132532.text: Which of the following disorders are caused due to recessive autosomal mutations?
options: Turner's syndrome and sickle cell anaemia
132532.sol: Cystic fibrosis is an abnormal recessive disorder of infants, children and young adults that is due to an abnormal recessive autosomal allele present on chromosome 7 . In 70 % of cases, it is due to deletion of three bases. The disease gets its name from the fibrous cysts that appear in the pancreas. It produces a defective glycoprotein. The defective glycoprotein causes formation of thick mucus in skin, lungs, pancreas, liver and other secretory organs. There is maldigestion of food with high fat content in stool.

132695.subject: Zoology
132695.text: What change occurred in the moth population after industrialization by 1920?
options: The population of white-winged moths increased
The population of dark-winged moths increased
The proportion of white-winged and dark-winged moths remained the same
Moth populations were no longer recorded
132695.sol: After industrialization by 1920, the population of dark-winged moths increased, reversing the earlier proportion observed before industrialization.During post- industrialisation period, the tree trunks became dark due to industrial smoke and soots. Under this condition the white-winged moth did not survive due to predators, dark-winged or melanised moth survived. Before industrialisation set in, thick growth of almost white-coloured lichen covered the trees - in that background the white winged moth survived but th

132948.subject: Zoology
132948.text: Observe the given evolutionary sequence leading to mammals: Early reptiles Synapsids Pelycosaurs [X] Mammals Identify the missing ancestor [X] and the geological era in which mammals first appeared on Earth.
132948.sol: According to the evolutionary history of vertebrates, the synapsid lineage gave rise to mammals. The correct sequence is: Early reptiles Synapsids Pelycosaurs Therapsids Mammals. Therefore, [X] is Therapsids. While mammals dominated the Earth during the Cenozoic era, they first originated much earlier during the Triassic period, which is a part of the Mesozoic era. Thecodonts belong to the sauropsid lineage, which led to dinosaurs, crocodiles, and birds, not mammals. Answer: [X] = Therapsids ; Era = Mesozoic

133403.subject: Zoology
133403.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Opioids such as heroin can cause significant addiction and health issues. Reason: Opioids bind to opioid receptors in the central nervous system, affecting pain and pleasure pathways.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133403.sol: Surveys and statistics show that use of drugs and alcohol has been on the rise especially among the youth. This is really a cause of concern as it could result in many harmful effects. Proper education and guidance would enable youth to safeguard themselves against these dangerous behaviour patterns and follow healthy lifestyles. The drugs, which are commonly abused are opioids, cannabinoids and coca alkaloids. Majority of these are obtained from flowering plants. Some are obtained from fungi. Opioids are the drugs

133710.subject: Zoology
133710.text: What is the traditional drink of some parts of southern India made from?
133710.sol: The dough, which is used for making foods such as dosa and idli is also fermented by bacteria. The puffed-up appearance of dough is due to the production of CO2 gas. The dough, which is used for making bread, is fermented using baker’s yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).A number of traditional drinks and foods are also made by fermentation by the microbes. ‘Toddy’, a traditional drink of some parts of southern India is made by fermenting sap from palms.

133712.subject: Zoology
133712.text: What gives Roquefort cheese its specific flavour?
options: The growth of a specific fungi
133712.sol: Cheese, is one of the oldest food items in which microbes were used. Different varieties of cheese are known by their characteristic texture, flavour and taste, the specificity coming from the microbes used. For example, the large holes in ‘Swiss cheese’ are due to production of a large amount of CO2 by a bacterium named Propionibacterium sharmanii. The ‘Roquefort cheese’ are ripened by growing a specific fungi on them, which gives them a particular flavour.

133905.subject: Zoology
133905.text: Microbe Use of the microbe A. Lactobacillus 1. Bread fermentation B. Saccharomyces 2. Vinegar production C. Acetobacter aceti 3. Curd formation D. Aspergillus niger 4. Citric acid production
133905.sol: Lactobacillus is used in the formation of curd. Saccharomyces (yeast) is used in the fermentation of bread. Acetobacter aceti is used in the production of vinegar. Aspergillus niger is used in the production of citric acid.

134059.subject: Zoology
134059.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134059.sol: Pebrine is a disease of silkworm caused by a small parasite. Nosema, which has a devastating effect on silk industry.

134421.subject: Zoology
134421.text: What is the definition of biotechnology according to the European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB)?
options: The integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof, and molecular analogues for products a
use of genetically modified organisms to produce biotechnological products on a larger scale
The preservation of genetic information through asexual reproduction
The use of traditional hybridization procedures in plant and animal breeding
134421.sol: Further, many other processes/techniques are also included under biotechnology. For example, in vitro fertilisation leading to a ‘test-tube’ baby, synthesising a gene and using it, developing a DNA vaccine or correcting a defective gene, are all part of biotechnology. The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) has given a definition of biotechnology that encompasses both traditional view and modern molecular biotechnology. The definition given by EFB is as follows: ‘The integration of natural science and organi

134978.subject: Zoology
134978.text: Stirred-tank bioreactors have been designed for:
options: Addition of preservatives to the product
Availability of oxygen throughout the process
Ensuring anaerobic conditions in the culture vessel
134978.sol: Stirred-tank bioreactor is provided with a stirrer for the availability of oxygen throughout the process. In stirred tank bioreactors, the air is bubbled through the reactor using a sparger. Air bubbles increase the surface area for transfer of oxygen and result in better mixing. The function of the agitation system is to increase mass transfer rates through the bulk liquid and bubble boundary layers by providing proper mixing.

135220.subject: Zoology
135220.text: What is the special adaptation by Mediterranean orchid Ophrys that ensure its pollination
options: Ophrys provides place to lay eggs on it
Ophrys provide nectar and portion for feeding its cocoon
135220.sol: The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs ‘sexual deceit’ to get pollination done by a species of bee. One petal of its flower bears an uncanny resemblance to the female of the bee in size, colour and markings.The male bee is attracted to what it perceives as a female, ‘pseudo copulates’ with the flower, and during that process is dusted with pollen from the flower.

135405.subject: Zoology
135405.text: Read the following statements regarding the symbolic representation of population interactions, where (+) denotes a beneficial interaction, (-) denotes a detrimental interaction, and (0) denotes a neutral interaction. Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In amensalism, one species is harmed whereas the other is unaffected, which is represented by a (-, 0) sign co
Both predation and parasitism are assigned a (+, -) sign convention because in both cases only one species ben
Commensalism is represented by (+, 0) since one interacting species derives a benefit while the other remains
Competition is represented by a (+, -) sign convention because the competitively superior species benefits whi
135405.sol: In population interactions, competition is defined as a process in which the fitness of one species is significantly lower in the presence of another species. It is detrimental to both species involved, regardless of which species is competitively superior. Therefore, competition is represented by a (-, -) sign convention, not (+, -) . The other statements are correct: Amensalism is (-, 0) as one species is harmed and the other is unaffected. Predation and parasitism are both (+, -) because one species benefits at

6a16f3287cfacf7984f86721.subject: Biology
6a16f3287cfacf7984f86721.text: As one moves away from the equator towards the poles, species diversity generally decreases. Based on this latitudinal gradient, which of the following regions harbours the lowest number of bird species?
6a16f3287cfacf7984f86721.sol: Species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles. Colombia is located near the equator and has about 1400 species of birds. India is mostly in the tropical region and has more than 1200 species of birds. New York is in the temperate region ( 41^ N) and has 105 species of birds. Greenland is in the polar region ( 71^ N) and has only 56 species of birds. Therefore, Greenland harbours the lowest number of bird species among the given regions. Answer: Greenland

6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a0f.subject: Biology
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a0f.text: Which of the following is a 'once a week' oral contraceptive pill for females that contains a non-steroidal preparation?
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a0f.sol: Saheli is an oral contraceptive pill for females that contains a non-steroidal preparation called centchroman. It is a 'once a week' pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value. Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs. Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD. Answer: Saheli

67efe2d75c97f0fe143c9904.subject: Biology
options: malignant tumours of the connective tissue
malignant tumours of the skin or mucous membrane
benign tumours of the connective tissue
67efe2d75c97f0fe143c9904.sol: Carcinoma refers to a malignant neoplasm of epithelial origin or cancer of the internal or external lining of the body. Carcinomas, malignancies of epithelial tissue, account for 80 to 90 percent of all cancer cases. Related Theory Carcinomas originate in the skin, lungs, breasts, pancreas, and other organs and glands. Lymphomas are cancers of lymphocytes. Leukaemia is cancer of the blood. It does not usually form solid tumours.

95805.sol: The main criteria of the five kingdom classification were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition and reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships. Monera includes bacteria and Ferns are included under Kingdom Plantae, Pteridophytes. Paramecium and Amoeba are placed in Kingdom Protista due to their unicellular nature. 96023.sol: Plastids are mainly of two types: (i) Coloured (including chromoplasts containing pigments other than chlorophyll and chloroplast containing green pigment chlorophyll). (ii) Leucoplasts, which store reserve food material, these are devoid of any pigment and may be carbohydrate storing amyloplast, lipid storing elaioplast or protein storing proteinoplast (aleuroplast).

Chromosome number 2 will have one chromatid with ab and another chromatid with aB. In anaphase 1, one of these chromosomes will go in one cell and the other will go in another cell. 96479.subject: Botany
96479.text: Which one of the following statements is correct for secondary succession?
options: It begins on a bare rock
It occurs on a deforested site
It is similar to primary succession except that it has a relatively fast pace
96479.sol: Secondary succession is one of the two types of ecological succession of a plants life. As opposed to the first, primary succession, secondary succession is a process started by an event (e.g. forest fire, harvesting, hurricane, etc.) that reduces an already established ecosystem (e.g. a forest or a wheat field) to a smaller population of species, and as such secondary succession occurs on preexisting soil whereas primary succession usually occurs in a place lacking soil.

96569.subject: Botany
96569.text: Which of the following constitutes of a micro-ecosystem?
96569.sol: A community of organisms interacting with abiotic component in a particular region/area will be called as ecosystem. The living and non-living components are linked together by the nutrient cycles and energy flow through each trophic level. Regions or locations defined by critical environmental factors within small spaces contain the micro-ecosystem. Pond is a classic example of microecosystem with limited water volume generally for short duration. These are generally colonized by organisms which are do not live in

96642.subject: Botany
96642.text: During decomposition, the process of mineralization by micro-organisms helps in the release of
options: inorganic nutrients from detritus and formation of humus
both organic and inorganic nutrients from detritus
96642.sol: Mineralization is the last step of decomposition, after humification, during which humus is formed. Humus is colloidal in nature which serves as a reservoir of inorganic nutrients. So, during mineralization inorganic nutrients are withdrawn with the help of microbes. At the level of detritus, fragmentation takes place due to which smaller particles are formed and during catabolism, detritus degrades into smaller inorganic substances with the help of bacterial and fungal enzymes.

96818.sol: China rose of Malvaceae family possess numerous stamens. The filaments of stamens are united in one group thus forming a staminal tube around the style. Such stamens are called monadelphous.

97124.subject: Botany
97124.text: Thalamus takes part in fruit formation in
97124.sol: Fruit that is formed from the fertilized ovary that surrounds the seeds. Such fruits are called true fruit. When the fruit part develops from other parts of the flower than the ovary is called as false fruit. True fruit is the fruit that is formed from the fertilized ovary of the flower and ovules get transformed into seeds. Strawberry develops from an aggregate of achenes and the edible part is thalamus. It is thus a false fruit.

97205.subject: Botany
97205.text: Growth of vascular cambium is an example of:
97205.sol: In arithmetic growth, the cell divides giving rise to two daughter cells. From which, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures to become a permanent cell. This kind of nature of growth rate is shown by meristematic cells. Plasticity is the ability of the tissues to form different structures in response to environmental conditions. Senescence is the deterioration phase with respect to the ageing of a cell or tissue or an organism.

97315.subject: Botany
97315.text: Which of the following is not a function of cytokinin?
97315.sol: It is a plant hormone that promotes cell division in plant roots and shoots.They are also involved in cell growth and differentiation. They also delay senescence in plants. It is also used for breaking the seed dormancy like in lettuce and tobacco etc. and induce seed germination. Abscisic acid promotes bud dormancy, not cytokinin.

97828.subject: Botany
options: A basic unit in the phylogenic history of living organisms
A group of related populations from evolutionary point of view
A basic category containing most of the taxonomic information
A population of similar characteristics which forms evolutionary basis of variation
97828.sol: Species is the smallest unit of taxonomic hierarchy, which consists of group of similar organism capable of interbreeding freely in nature to form fertile offsprings. It brings about variation necessary for evolution.

97966.subject: Botany
97966.text: When a solute is mixed, the water potential of the cell
97966.sol: Water molecules possess kinetic energy. In liquid and gaseous form they are in random motion that is both rapid and constant. The greater the concentration of water in a system, the greater is its kinetic energy or water potential. If some solute is dissolved in pure water, the solution has fewer free water and the concentration of water decreases, reducing its water potential.

306823.text: A magnetic field fails to cause deflection in
306823.sol: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic waves and do not carry any charge. The magnetic force on a moving particle is given by F = q( v B ) . Since the charge q = 0 for gamma rays, the magnetic force acting on them is zero. Alpha rays are positively charged, beta-minus rays are negatively charged, and beta-plus rays are positively charged, so they all experience a magnetic force and are deflected. Therefore, a magnetic field fails to cause deflection in gamma rays.
